__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Prometheus data source scraping the orleans.lattice (and optionally orleans.lattice.replication) meter.

panels.title: Cluster throughput (ops/s)
panels.description: Cluster-wide read and write OPERATION rate. Both series count operations, not records: a batched or bulk write counts once regardless of entry count. See 'Per-tree write throughput (operations/s and records/s)' for the record rate.

panels.title: Per-tree write throughput (operations/s and records/s)
panels.description: Two distinct semantics, deliberately plotted together. 'ops' is orleans_lattice_shard_writes, incremented once per write OPERATION: a batched or bulk operation (SetManyAsync, MergeManyAsync, DeleteRangeAsync, BulkLoadAsync, BulkLoadRawAsync, BulkAppendAsync) counts once regardless of entry count. 'records' is orleans_lattice_shard_records_written, incremented by the entry count of each operation. On OLTP-style single-key traffic the two lines coincide; a bulk import shows a large records spike against an almost flat ops line, and the ratio between them is the effective batch size. Reading 'ops' alone under-represents bulk ingestion.

panels.title: Leaf scan duration p95 by operation
Consolidations committed (rate)
panels.description: Rate of online shard consolidations committed (orleans.lattice.shard.consolidations_committed), by tree. Each increment is one donor shard retired from the routing map, counted only after the fold's terminal state write is durable. This is the inverse of Splits committed: compare the two to tell a tree that is actually healing from one whose physical shard count is still climbing.

panels.title: Healing backlog (shards above base)
panels.description: Physical shards each tree carries above its configured base shard count (orleans.lattice.shard.healing.backlog), sampled once per automatic over-split healing sweep. This is the healing work outstanding: a tree is healed exactly when its series reaches zero, so the count of series at zero is the number of trees healed. Read it with Consolidations committed - backlog says how much damage is left, that panel says whether it is going down. A backlog that is flat and non-zero while Healing decisions shows skewed_load, backpressure, or cooldown is a tree that needs healing and is deliberately being held back, not a stuck orchestrator.

panels.title: Healing decisions by outcome
panels.description: Automatic over-split healing sweeps by decision (orleans.lattice.shard.healing.decisions), one increment per tree per sweep. The series currently advancing for a tree is that tree's current healing decision. not_over_split is the healthy steady state; admitted means a fold was started this sweep; skewed_load, backpressure, cooldown, split_in_flight, tree_maintenance and at_capacity are deliberate hold-backs; disabled and admission_closed mean the mechanism is switched off. Use it to tell a tree that never heals because it never needed to from one that never heals because something is blocking it.

panels.title: Events dropped (by reason)
panels.description: Conditionally-emitted series here (events.dropped) carry no 'or vector(0)' zero-fill: they are recorded only when their condition occurs, so an empty result means that condition never arose. Absence is the healthy reading on those series, not a measured zero (issue #2520).

panels.title: Active shards (per tree)
panels.description: Distinct shard count per tree over time, derived from observed orleans_lattice_shard_reads_total series. Respects the Tree / Cluster / Silo filters.

panels.title: Atomic write saga duration (p50/p95/p99 ms)
panels.description: End-to-end SetManyAtomicAsync saga duration captured from Prepare to Completed. Reflects true wall-clock cost including any reminder-driven recovery time. Tag dimensions: tree, outcome.

panels.title: Atomic write batch size (p50/p95/p99 entries)
panels.description: Entry count of each SetManyAtomicAsync saga at terminal transition. Pair with saga duration to detect distribution shifts in caller batch sizing.

panels.title: Atomic write saga failure rate (%)
panels.description: Fraction of terminal SetManyAtomicAsync sagas that did not reach the committed outcome. Sums failed + compensated rates and divides by the total terminal-transition rate. A non-zero floor here indicates either contention surfacing as compensation (possibly healthy) or surrogate failures (always investigate).

panels.title: Compaction pass duration p95 (ms, by trigger)
panels.description: End-to-end RunCompactionPassAsync wall-clock duration split by trigger source: reminder-driven baseline passes, ratio/size policy-trigger passes, and operator-initiated passes. A divergence between trigger labels means policy passes are markedly cheaper or more expensive than baseline passes - investigate the policy thresholds.

panels.title: Compaction leaves visited (rate, by outcome)
panels.description: Per-leaf compaction outcome rate: 'reaped' means at least one tombstone was physically removed, 'noop' means the leaf had pending tombstones that were still inside the grace window. A high noop:reaped ratio suggests TombstoneGracePeriod is too long for the workload's tombstone-to-write ratio.

panels.title: Compaction shard retries / skips (rate)
panels.description: Coordinator-level resilience signal. Retries indicate transient leaf-walk failures that the coordinator absorbed. Skips indicate shards the coordinator gave up on after exhausting retries - a non-zero skip rate is an alert-worthy condition.

panels.title: Leaf tombstone ratio p95
panels.description: Distribution of tombstone-to-live-entry ratio sampled per mutation. The p95 is the headroom signal for MinTombstoneRatioForCompaction: when p95 trends above the configured threshold, the ratio policy will start firing out-of-cycle compaction passes.

panels.title: Storage footprint by tree
panels.description: Byte-accurate retained footprint per tree, broken down by surface: WAL bytes, snapshot blob bytes, and summed leaf/shard-root state bytes. Sourced from the observable storage-usage gauges; a tree on an unsupported provider reports no data rather than a misleading zero. The snapshot and leaf-state series additionally report no data until the tree has had a deep storage-usage publish, which only an explicit ILatticeAdmin.RefreshStorageUsageAsync or ILattice.GetStorageUsageAsync call drives - the continuous background poller measures WAL bytes only. So a tree showing a WAL line and no snapshot or leaf-state line has not been measured on those surfaces; consult 'Storage usage measurement depth by tree' before reading their absence as emptiness (issue #2693). Each tree's footprint is published by a single per-tree aggregator on whichever one silo currently hosts it, so this panel deliberately ignores the $silo selector and sums across all silos in the selected cluster - filtering by silo would hide every tree whose aggregator lives elsewhere.

panels.title: Cluster total retained bytes
panels.description: Single stat summing orleans_lattice_storage_total_bytes across every tree and silo: the cluster-wide byte-accurate footprint of all Lattice storage surfaces. Storage gauges are emitted on exactly one silo per tree, so this stat ignores the $silo selector and sums across all silos in the selected cluster. A tree contributes nothing here until it has had a deep storage-usage publish, because the total omits two of its three terms otherwise; check 'Storage usage measurement depth by tree' to tell an unmeasured tree from an empty one (issue #2693).

panels.title: Storage usage measurement depth by tree
panels.description: 1 when the tree's last storage-usage report came from the deep path that actually measures snapshot and leaf-state bytes, 0 when only the cheap WAL-only background poller has reported (orleans.lattice.storage.usage_deep_published). Read this panel BEFORE reading the snapshot / leaf-state / total series above: those three report no data rather than a synthesised 0 until a deep publish has run, and the deep path runs only on an explicit ILatticeAdmin.RefreshStorageUsageAsync or ILattice.GetStorageUsageAsync call. A tree sitting at 0 here means those panels are 'not measured', not 'measured empty'. Before issue #2693 the poller seeded them to 0 without measuring them, and a reader took that zero as a measurement and concluded no leaf state or snapshots were ever written while 137 MB of snapshot state was on disk (issue #2692). Published by the same single per-tree aggregator as the storage-footprint panels, so it lands on one silo per tree and this panel ignores the $silo selector.

panels.title: Trees over advisory threshold
panels.description: Trees whose retained WAL bytes currently breach the advisory ceiling (LatticeOptions.WalMaxRetainedBytes). The 0/1 over_threshold gauge stays at 1 while a lagging consumer pins bytes the byte-pressure policy cannot safely reclaim - the breach is advisory and the durability invariant wins. The over_threshold gauge is published by the same single per-tree aggregator as the storage-footprint panels, so it lands on one silo per tree; this panel deliberately ignores the $silo selector and evaluates across all silos in the selected cluster, otherwise a breaching tree would be hidden whenever its aggregator is placed on an unselected silo.

panels.title: Byte-pressure trim activity
panels.description: Rate of advisory byte-pressure trim passes (policy.trim_triggered, reason=byte_pressure) and the WAL bytes those passes reclaimed (policy.bytes_reclaimed). A non-zero trigger rate with a flat reclaim rate means consumers are lagging and the bytes could not be safely freed. These counters accrue in each tree's WAL partition grain - a single activation per partition - so they land on one silo per partition; this panel deliberately ignores the $silo selector and sums across all silos in the selected cluster rather than tracking which silo currently hosts a partition grain.

panels.title: WAL compression savings ratio by tree
panels.description: Fraction of encoded WAL payload bytes saved by the Azure Table provider's per-row compression, per tree: 1 - rate(stored_bytes) / rate(uncompressed_bytes). 0 means no saving (every row stored verbatim); higher is better. Reads as no data for a tree with no WAL append traffic in the window, since the ratio is undefined with no bytes. Pair with the skips-by-reason panel to the right to explain a low ratio. The provider compression counters accrue in each tree's WAL partition grain (a single activation per partition), so they land on one silo per partition; this ratio deliberately ignores the $silo selector and is computed across all silos in the selected cluster - a per-silo view would only reflect which partition grains are currently placed there, not a per-silo compression property.

panels.title: WAL compression skips by reason
panels.description: Rate of WAL rows the Azure Table provider stored verbatim instead of compressed, by reason: below_threshold (payload shorter than CompressionMinPayloadBytes), inflation_guard (compressing did not shrink it), or disabled (compression off). A low savings ratio dominated by below_threshold is the cue to lower CompressionMinPayloadBytes; one dominated by inflation_guard means the payloads are incompressible and lowering it would only burn CPU. Like the savings-ratio panel, these counters accrue in each tree's WAL partition grain (a single activation per partition), so they land on one silo per partition; this panel deliberately ignores the $silo selector and sums across all silos in the selected cluster rather than tracking partition-grain placement.

panels.title: GetAsync / GetManyAsync envelope p50 (ms)
panels.description: Top-of-stack public-API read-call duration: get.duration is single-key GetAsync, get_many.duration is batched GetManyAsync. Pair with the cache hit-ratio panel above (cache.hits / cache.misses) to interpret in context - on a hot keyspace the LeafCacheGrain serves most reads in the tens-of-microseconds range; on a cache-miss-heavy workload the envelope grows by one cross-grain RPC into the primary leaf.

panels.title: GetAsync / GetManyAsync envelope p95 / p99 (ms)
panels.description: p95 and p99 of the public-API read-call envelopes. The gap between p50 and p99 is the tail introduced by stale-routing retries, registry-snapshot retries, topology-version drift mid-fan-out, or LeafCacheGrain TTL-driven delta refreshes.

panels.title: GetAsync stage breakdown p95 (ms)
panels.description: Per-stage sub-attribution inside LatticeGrain.GetAsync. get.stage.duration is tagged stage = route (per-attempt GetShardGrainAsync resolution) and stage = shard (per-attempt shard.GetAsync RPC including the cache-or-leaf read). Under a stale-routing storm both stages record multiple observations per envelope so the histograms attribute the retry cost. Conditionally-emitted series here (get.stage.duration) carry no 'or vector(0)' zero-fill: they are recorded only when their condition occurs, so an empty result means that condition never arose. Absence is the healthy reading on those series, not a measured zero (issue #2520).

panels.title: GetManyAsync stage breakdown p95 (ms)
panels.description: Per-stage sub-attribution inside LatticeGrain.GetManyAsync. get_many.stage.duration is tagged stage in {route, bucket, fanout, merge}, isolating routing fetch, per-key shard bucketing, the cross-shard parallel fan-out (registry snapshot + Task.WhenAll), and the trailing topology / snap2 stability checks plus dictionary materialise.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, stage) (rate(orleans_lattice_get_many_stage_duration_milliseconds_bucket{tree=~"$tree",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: ExistsAsync / GetWithVersionAsync envelope p95 (ms)
panels.description: Lower-traffic read surfaces: exists.duration (key-existence probe) and get_with_version.duration (versioned point read). GetWithVersionAsync bypasses the LeafCacheGrain by design - the returned HybridLogicalClock must reflect the primary leaf's authoritative ordering - so this envelope runs systematically higher than the cached GetAsync envelope above on the same key distribution. If that ordering inverts on a dashboard, treat it as a regression signal.

panels.title: WAL saturation regime - current state per tree
panels.description: Step-plot of the per-tree WAL saturation state observable gauge (orleans.lattice.wal.saturation.state). Values: 0 = Healthy (normal traffic), 1 = Throttled (per-partition admission depth at-or-above WalSaturationThrottledRatio, default 0.75 - callers should slow down but appends still land), 2 = Saturated (admission cap reached with parked callers, OR recent dispatch-timeout trips OR provider-failure rate crossed the configured thresholds - callers should pause new appends). A sustained non-zero series is the leading-edge surface for the WAL back-pressure regime the silo cannot otherwise expose to operators without a live SSH session. Pair with the transition counters below for direction attribution.

panels.title: WAL saturation regime - transition rate by direction (ops/s)
panels.description: Per-direction transition rate on the orleans.lattice.wal.saturation.transitions counter, broken out by the new state tag. Each series shows how often the classifier flips into the named state per second. A rising rate of state=throttled is the leading edge of the saturation regime; state=saturated is the regime itself; state=healthy is the recovery edge. Flapping between Throttled and Saturated at a high frequency is a different operational signal from a sustained Saturated regime - the latter is the genuine cap, the former is the bursty per-partition WAL drain pattern (defended against by WalSaturationRecoveryWindow).

panels.title: WAL saturation regime - per-partition attribution (heat-map)
panels.description: Per-partition transition-rate heat-map on the orleans.lattice.wal.saturation.transitions counter, grouped by the partition tag. Identifies which underlying WAL partition is driving the regime when one partition's drain pattern dominates the tree's worst-case rollup. A solitary hot partition is the canonical pattern under the single-account 409-Conflict regime (the 409s back up against the partition the SDK chose; the others stay clear). A spread across every partition indicates a true cluster-wide cap saturation. Transitions without a partition tag (provider-failure-rate triggered, attributed by shard rather than partition) appear as the empty label series.

panels.title: WAL saturation regime - % time non-Healthy (1h)
panels.description: Per-tree fraction of the last hour the tree spent in a non-Healthy regime (Throttled or Saturated), as a percentage. A one-tile KPI suitable for at-a-glance dashboards: 0% = the tree never left Healthy; 100% = the tree has been continuously back-pressured for the full hour. Intermediate values quantify how much of the operational hour the silo was telling callers to slow down. Uses avg_over_time on the state observable gauge (values 0/1/2 ordered as Healthy<Throttled<Saturated) divided by 2 to normalise to [0, 1] then multiplied by 100. Operationally: <5% is the steady-state target for a non-saturating workload; sustained values above ~20% are the cue to raise WalMaxPendingBatches, the storage account count (F-084), or the offered load.

panels.title: Snapshot replay throughput (rate)
panels.description: Rate of entries replayed from snapshots (orleans.lattice.snapshot.replay.entries), by tree. Non-zero during activation/recovery when a leaf rebuilds state from a snapshot plus WAL tail. Conditionally-emitted series here (snapshot.replay.entries) carry no 'or vector(0)' zero-fill: they are recorded only when their condition occurs, so an empty result means that condition never arose. Absence is the healthy reading on those series, not a measured zero (issue #2520).

panels.title: Snapshot replay duration p50/p95/p99 (ms)
panels.description: Wall-clock duration of snapshot replay operations (orleans.lattice.snapshot.replay.duration). Long tails extend activation latency for cold leaves.

panels.title: Snapshot pins (current)
panels.description: Current number of pinned snapshots (orleans.lattice.snapshot.pins observable gauge, derived from the WAL cursor registry). Pins hold a snapshot alive against trimming. The gauge reports only the pins held now, so a value that climbs and does not come back down is a real pin leak rather than accumulated metric drift.

panels.title: Retroactive split-forward throughput (rate)
panels.description: Rate of entries retroactively forwarded to a sibling shard after an adaptive split (orleans.lattice.split.retroactive_forward.entries), by tree. Non-zero only while a split is reconciling writes that landed on the pre-split slot ownership. Conditionally-emitted series here (split.retroactive_forward.entries) carry no 'or vector(0)' zero-fill: they are recorded only when their condition occurs, so an empty result means that condition never arose. Absence is the healthy reading on those series, not a measured zero (issue #2520).

panels.title: Retroactive split-forward duration p50/p95/p99 (ms)
panels.description: Wall-clock duration of retroactive split-forward operations (orleans.lattice.split.retroactive_forward.duration). Bounded by the split coordinators leaf-chain drain.

panels.title: Compaction dirty leaves per pass (p50/p95)
panels.description: Distribution of dirty leaves visited per compaction pass (orleans.lattice.compaction.shard.dirty_leaves). A rising distribution means compaction is falling behind the write rate. Conditionally-emitted series here (compaction.shard.dirty_leaves) carry no 'or vector(0)' zero-fill: they are recorded only when their condition occurs, so an empty result means that condition never arose. Absence is the healthy reading on those series, not a measured zero (issue #2520).

panels.title: Auto-trained dictionary - training runs by outcome (rate)
panels.description: Rate of auto-trained shared-dictionary training-pass attempts on the orleans.lattice.compress.dictionary.training_runs counter, split by outcome: trained (a dictionary was built), skipped_insufficient_samples (the reservoir held too few samples or the builder rejected the corpus), or skipped_cadence (the minimum training interval had not elapsed). A flat zero means auto-training is disabled or no host is driving training passes. A series dominated by skipped_insufficient_samples is the cue to lower MinSamplesToTrain or raise the sampling rate; one dominated by skipped_cadence means passes are being attempted faster than MinTrainingInterval allows.

panels.title: Auto-trained dictionary - active version
panels.description: Current active auto-trained dictionary id (orleans.lattice.compress.dictionary.active_version observable gauge), per silo. 0 means no dictionary has been trained yet. A step up marks a successful training roll-over; a monotonically rising series across a long window indicates frequent re-training (each roll-over bumps the version id). The id is the version the encoder requests; recent prior versions stay resolvable so in-flight frames against a just-superseded version still decompress.

panels.title: Auto-trained dictionary - reservoir fill
panels.description: Auto-training reservoir occupancy (orleans.lattice.compress.dictionary.reservoir_fill observable gauge), split by kind: samples (retained sample count) and bytes (retained total bytes). Both are bounded by MaxSampleCount and MaxReservoirBytes; a series pinned at the cap with a healthy training-run rate is normal steady state. A samples series stuck below MinSamplesToTrain explains a training_runs panel dominated by skipped_insufficient_samples.

panels.title: Auto-trained dictionary - trained vs baseline compression ratio
panels.description: Trained-dictionary compressed size as a fraction of the no-dictionary (plain Zstd) baseline on the training probe: rate(trained_bytes_out) / rate(trained_bytes_in). Below 1 means the auto-trained dictionary beats plain Zstd on the sampled corpus (lower is better); at or above 1 means the dictionary is not helping and the corpus may be too heterogeneous to train a useful shared dictionary. Reads as no data when no training pass has completed in the window.

panels.title: Admission - live keys by tree
panels.description: Current live (non-tombstone) key count per tree (orleans_lattice_admission_live_keys observable gauge). This is the figure per-tree admission control compares against LatticeOptions.MaxLiveKeys. Best-effort and eventually-consistent: it is the same cached, TTL-coalesced per-tree aggregate that backs the storage-footprint panels, published by a single per-tree aggregator, so it lands on one silo per tree; this panel deliberately ignores the $silo selector and evaluates across all silos in the selected cluster. Step 1 of the adoption workflow: watch this to learn a tree's steady-state live-key count before setting any ceiling.

panels.title: Admission - estimated bytes by tree
panels.description: Current estimated retained bytes per tree (orleans_lattice_admission_estimated_bytes observable gauge), the figure admission control compares against LatticeOptions.MaxEstimatedBytes. Aliases the storage total-bytes figure (WAL rows plus snapshot blobs plus leaf/shard-root state). Published by the same single per-tree aggregator as the live-keys panel, so it lands on one silo per tree; this panel ignores the $silo selector and evaluates across all silos in the selected cluster. Step 1 of the adoption workflow for the byte dimension: watch this to learn a tree's steady-state footprint before setting a ceiling.

panels.title: Admission - trees over advisory ceiling
panels.description: Trees currently exceeding an advisory admission ceiling (AdmissionAdvisoryLiveKeys or AdmissionAdvisoryBytes). The 0/1 over_advisory gauge is 1 while the tree's live-key count or estimated bytes sits at or above its advisory ceiling; the ceiling is non-enforcing, so no write is rejected. Published by the single per-tree aggregator, so it lands on one silo per tree; this panel ignores the $silo selector and evaluates across all silos in the selected cluster. Step 3 of the adoption workflow: watch this while an advisory ceiling is set to see whether the tree would breach a candidate cap.

panels.title: Admission - would-reject rate (advisory dry-run)
panels.description: Rate of writes that WOULD have been rejected at a tree's advisory admission ceiling, by dimension (orleans_lattice_admission_would_reject_total, tagged tree and dimension = keys | bytes). No write is actually rejected: this is the dry-run blast radius of a candidate cap. These counters accrue at the write boundary (a per-silo stateless worker), so this panel sums across all silos in the selected cluster. Step 3 of the adoption workflow: a non-zero rate here tells you a promoted enforcing cap at the current advisory ceiling would start rejecting that many writes.

panels.title: Admission - utilization by dimension
panels.description: Current admission utilisation ratio (current / ceiling) per tree and dimension (orleans_lattice_admission_utilization observable gauge, tagged tree and dimension = keys | bytes). The denominator prefers the enforcing cap (MaxLiveKeys / MaxEstimatedBytes) and falls back to the advisory ceiling when only that is set; a series is emitted only for a dimension whose ceiling is configured. At or above 1 means the enforcing cap is being hit and writes on that dimension are being rejected. Published by the single per-tree aggregator, so this panel ignores the $silo selector and evaluates across all silos in the selected cluster. Step 4 of the adoption workflow: watch this after promoting a ceiling to an enforcing cap.

panels.title: Admission - rejected write rate (enforced)
panels.description: Rate of writes actually rejected by an enforced admission cap, by dimension (orleans_lattice_admission_rejected_total, tagged tree and dimension = keys | bytes). Each increment corresponds to a LatticeQuotaExceededException thrown at the write boundary. These counters accrue at the write boundary (a per-silo stateless worker), so this panel sums across all silos in the selected cluster. Step 4 of the adoption workflow: this is the ground-truth signal that enforcement is live and which trees are being throttled.

panels.title: Distributed lock - acquire / release / reclaim rate
panels.description: Throughput of the FIFO-fair distributed lock (ILatticeLockGrain). orleans_lattice_lock_acquired_total is tagged outcome = granted | timeout | unavailable (a granted acquire, a wait-timeout or non-blocking miss, and a TryAcquire on a held lock respectively); orleans_lattice_lock_released_total counts explicit releases; orleans_lattice_lock_lease_reclaimed_total counts leases reclaimed after a holder let its lease expire without renewing. A rising reclaim rate means holders are crashing or failing to renew before expiry.

panels.title: Distributed lock - acquire wait latency
panels.description: Time a contended acquire spent parked in the FIFO queue before it was granted, from orleans_lattice_lock_acquire_wait_milliseconds (recorded once per grant, so an uncontended acquire records ~0). p50 / p95 / p99 over the selected cluster. A rising tail indicates deep lock contention or holders holding leases for their full duration.

panels.title: Atomic action - saga and step rate
panels.description: Throughput of the generic atomic-action (saga / TCC) coordinator (IAtomicActionGrain). orleans_lattice_atomic_action_completed_total is tagged outcome = committed | compensated | compensation_failed (every forward step committed, a forward fault cleanly rolled back, or a compensating effect itself faulted and parked the saga); orleans_lattice_atomic_action_step_total is tagged phase = forward | compensate and outcome = ok | fault, counting each step effect. A rising compensated or compensation_failed rate means forward effects are faulting; a non-zero compensate/fault rate means the caller's compensation contract is being violated.

panels.title: Atomic action - saga duration
panels.description: End-to-end atomic-action saga duration from orleans_lattice_atomic_action_duration_milliseconds (recorded once per terminal transition, measured from saga start so it includes time suspended across silo restarts). p50 / p95 / p99 over the selected cluster. A rising tail on the compensated series indicates expensive rollbacks.

panels.title: Outstanding calls per target activation, by grain type
panels.description: Per-grain-type contention from orleans_lattice_grain_call_outstanding_depth, recorded at dispatch on EVERY outgoing grain call by the LatticeGrainCallObservationFilter (enable with ISiloBuilder.AddLatticeGrainCallObservation). The value is how many calls this silo had already issued to the same target activation and not yet seen complete, so on a non-reentrant target it is the depth the new call queues behind. Read this instead of the NonReentrancyQueueSize= clause of the Orleans near-timeout diagnostic: that clause is emitted only for a request already approaching the 30s deadline and describes only that request's own wait, so a grain type that queues deeply without tripping the timeout contributes nothing to it. Two known limits: the count is per-silo, so cluster-wide contention is under-stated (treat it as a floor), and on a reentrant or AlwaysInterleave target a high value means pipelining rather than queueing.

panels.title: Grain-call duration by grain type and outcome
panels.description: orleans_lattice_grain_call_duration_milliseconds, recorded by the same filter for every outgoing grain call and tagged outcome = completed | faulted. Split by outcome deliberately: the faulted series carries the 30s message timeouts, which would otherwise pile up at the deadline and dominate any quantile taken over the combined population - the same censoring that makes the near-timeout log diagnostic unusable for sizing a queue. Compare against the outstanding-depth panel: rising duration WITH rising depth is contention on the target; rising duration with flat depth is the target itself getting slower.

panels.title: Coordinator phase-tick failures (rate)
panels.description: Rate of coordinator phase-timer ticks that threw and were swallowed by the phase loop (orleans_lattice_coordinator_phase_tick_failures_total), split by the coordinator kind and the tree it drives. Each such tick is a phase of work the coordinator began and discarded: the loop absorbs the fault and re-arms, so throughput degrades silently and no other series moves. Before this counter existed the only trace was a log line, and 35 failures over 516 minutes on the acceptance rig left every exported series flat - which is what issue #2705 was filed for. The counter is zero-primed for every coordinator when its phase timer starts, so a flat line at zero is a positive reading that ticks are succeeding, NOT an absent series; 'No data' here means the coordinator never started, which is itself worth investigating. Any sustained non-zero rate is operator-actionable, and the emitting grain escalates its own log from warning to error after three consecutive failures - so correlate a step here with the error-level log to find the failing coordinator.

panels.title: Leaf division fast path forfeited (rate)
panels.description: Rate of leaf splits that could not place their pivot from the snapshot frame and fell back to materialising the whole leaf (orleans_lattice_leaf_bisect_refusals_total), split by the refusal reason and by the cache surface that had already released the frame. Read the two tags together - the reason alone cannot tell a benign refusal from a harmful one. reason=no_snapshot_attached with detach_seam=none is benign: no frame was ever attached (a leaf replayed from the WAL), the leaf is already resident, and the fallback costs nothing extra. The SAME reason with any other detach_seam is the defect (issue #2787): a frame WAS attached and an unrelated whole-leaf operation consumed it, so the division must now make every row resident and unsheddable for the life of the activation - on precisely the oversized leaf that can least afford the allocation, and the operation that would have reduced its size. The refusal is a function of activation history, not of leaf size, so the split seam itself cannot distinguish the two cases and this counter is the only place the forfeiture is observable. Any sustained non-zero rate carrying a detach_seam other than 'none' is operator-actionable, and names the seam to convert.

targets.expr: sum by (tree, reason, detach_seam) (rate(orleans_lattice_leaf_bisect_refusals_total{tree=~"$tree",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Leaf divisions sought (rate)
panels.description: Rate of divisions SOUGHT on an over-capacity leaf (orleans_lattice_leaf_split_attempts_total), split by outcome: divided (the division ran to completion), gate_contended (another turn held the split gate, so this turn returned without evaluating the leaf), already_under_capacity (the in-gate re-check found the leaf back under threshold because a concurrent turn had divided it). Read this BESIDE the bisect-refusal panel, which is uninterpretable alone. A zero refusal rate has two opposite meanings - no division ever forfeited its fast path, or no division was ever attempted - and only the attempt count separates them. That distinction is the whole question on an oversized leaf: a leaf sitting far above MaxLeafBytes with zero refusals AND zero attempts is not a leaf whose splits are succeeding, it is a leaf nothing is trying to split, which is a different defect with a different fix. All three outcomes are pre-minted at zero whenever a leaf reaches the byte-bound check on the snapshot-capture path, carrying the tag set a real emission carries, so this panel deliberately OMITS the 'or vector(0)' fallback its neighbours use: a flat zero here is a MEASURED zero and 'No data' means the capture seam was never reached, which is itself the finding. Sustained gate_contended with no divided is the pathological shape - divisions are being sought and none is completing.

panels.title: Coordinator consecutive phase-tick failure run
panels.description: Length of the CURRENT run of consecutive failed phase ticks per coordinator kind and tree (orleans_lattice_coordinator_phase_tick_consecutive_failures), as the maximum over the activations sharing a tag set. Read it BESIDE the phase-tick failure rate panel, which cannot answer this question: a cumulative counter has no notion of consecutiveness, so a coordinator failing one tick in a thousand and one that has failed every tick since the process started both present as a rising rate - yet the first is a transient the loop absorbs by design and the second is a phase machine that has stopped advancing and will not resume without intervention. That distinction is what issue #2814 turned on, and the only evidence for it was the phrase '156 times in a row' in a 53 MB log stream. Every live coordinator reports, enrolling at zero when its phase timer arms, so this panel deliberately OMITS the 'or vector(0)' fallback its neighbours use: a flat zero is a MEASURED zero meaning the last tick succeeded, and 'No data' means no coordinator of that kind is live, which is itself the finding. A series that keeps returning to zero is a coordinator absorbing transients; one that only climbs is a wedge, and its value is how many ticks of work have been discarded back to back. A zero does NOT mean the coordinator is progressing - a tick that returns without advancing its phase machine is a success by this measure.

panels.title: Leaf-split completions in flight
panels.description: Count of leaf-split completions currently suspended inside CompleteSplitAsync per tree (orleans_lattice_leaf_split_completion_in_flight, issue #2967). The divided/faulted outcome counters partition only TERMINATED divisions, so a division still in the completion body at scrape time is a member of none of them, and because the catch that records faulted is unconditional a division carrying neither divided nor faulted did not throw - it is genuinely in flight. Read this BESIDE the oldest-completion-age panel: a non-zero count is only actionable once that age is climbing. A tree with nothing in flight emits no series, so 'No data' is the healthy steady state, not a gap.

panels.title: Oldest leaf-split completion age
panels.description: Age in seconds of the oldest leaf-split completion currently suspended inside CompleteSplitAsync per tree (orleans_lattice_leaf_split_completion_oldest_age, issue #2967). This is the signal that separates a division momentarily in flight (age near zero, falling as scrapes advance) from one that is STUCK (age climbing without bound), which the bare in-flight count cannot do. It is a measurement, not a threshold: the code encodes no age at which a completion is declared abandoned, so alert on a sustained climb read against real completion durations rather than on a fixed value. A tree with nothing in flight emits no series, so 'No data' is the healthy steady state.

panels.title: Tree-registry singleton - service time and fan-in width
panels.description: The tree registry is one activation for the whole cluster, addressed by every per-tree background service, so a cold start fans the whole estate onto it. When it saturates, callers see only a 30s response-deadline TimeoutException - and that same observation is produced both by a call served slowly and by a call never served at all, which have opposite remedies. registry.call.duration records only calls the grain actually ADMITTED, so read its tail together with its rate against the caller-side timeout count: a short tail whose rate is far below the offered load means the calls never reached the body at all (blocked in activation, or behind a turn that never yielded - neither of which an [AlwaysInterleave] attribute admits past), while a tail approaching the caller deadline at a matching rate means they were admitted and the time went on the awaited hop to the backing _lattice_trees tree. registry.call.in_flight is the fan-in WIDTH at the moment each call is admitted, excluding the arriving call: a long tail over a flat-zero width is a slow backing hop, whereas a width that climbs with estate size is the (trees x per-tree background services) scaling law saturating one activation. Both are platform-tenant series - the registry spans every tenant, so there is no per-tree breakdown to filter.

panels.title: Tree-registry fan-in gate - admission wait
panels.description: Time a tree id waited for a fan-in permit before its batched registry read was dispatched (orleans_lattice_registry_admission_wait, issue #3240). Cold-start fan-in onto the registry singleton is bounded by RegistryFanInGate, and bounding fan-in does not remove work - it queues it. That matters for reading every other panel on this dashboard: once concurrent reads are capped, a saturated registry stops producing registry-side symptoms and starts producing caller-side waiting instead, so registry.call.duration, registry.call.in_flight and the caller-side timeout count all fall toward zero and the estate reads as recovered. This panel is the only place that relocated wait is visible. Read it AGAINST the service-time panel: a rising wait together with a rising registry.call.duration is a slow registry, which is the expected shape under genuine load, whereas a rising wait with registry.call.duration flat means the GATE is what callers are queueing on rather than the registry. Admission is deliberately uncapped and untimed - shedding a cold-start options resolution would turn latency into a correctness failure, since the caller cannot proceed without its entry - so unbounded waiting is a reachable state and nothing else would reveal it. Recorded on every dequeue including a zero wait, so the rate is the gated-read rate and a flat-zero mean is the healthy steady state rather than a gap. A platform-tenant series: the registry spans every tenant, so there is no per-tree breakdown to filter. Conditionally-emitted series here (registry.admission.wait) carry no 'or vector(0)' zero-fill: they are recorded only when their condition occurs, so an empty result means that condition never arose. Absence is the healthy reading on those series, not a measured zero (issue #2520).

panels.title: Tree-registry calls - caller-observed duration and outcome
panels.description: How long each ILatticeRegistry call took as seen by its CALLER, by interface method and outcome (orleans_lattice_registry_caller_duration, issue #3088). Recorded on every silo by an always-on outgoing call filter, for every registry call dispatched, whatever became of it - so unlike registry.call.duration, which only sees calls the grain admitted, it also records the calls that were never served. That is what separates the three readings the Orleans timeout diagnostic used to be relied on for, and which it stops providing under saturation (its CurrentlyExecuting block vanishes silo-wide, and its absence reads as an idle registry). Every series is split by method AND outcome. FINE: only completed series, with a short mean. SLOW: completed series with a long mean. UNREACHABLE: a timeout series appears, its mean pinned at the response deadline - and a timeout series on a method here while the service-time panel shows no admitted calls for it means those calls were never served, not served slowly. Timeout samples sit at the deadline, which is why timeout is its own outcome rather than folded into the completed distribution. Per-silo, and a platform-tenant series: the registry spans every tenant, so there is no per-tree breakdown to filter. Conditionally-emitted series here carry no 'or vector(0)' zero-fill: a timeout or faulted series exists only once such a call occurred, so its absence is the healthy reading, not a measured zero (issue #2520).

targets.expr: sum by (method, outcome) (rate(orleans_lattice_registry_caller_duration_milliseconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m])) / sum by (method, outcome) (rate(orleans_lattice_registry_caller_duration_milliseconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m]))

panels.title: Deployed build (version / commit)
panels.description: Silo count per distinct running build identity (orleans_lattice_build_info). This is the only instrument in the estate that answers 'is the build under test the build that is actually running'. Every other metric here reports something a feature did, so each is silent until that feature is exercised, which makes a missing series ambiguous between 'the image did not deploy' and 'the code deployed but that path was never reached'. This series is emitted unconditionally from process start with a constant value of 1, so its absence means the process is not running or not exporting, and means nothing else. More than one row means the estate is running mixed builds, which invalidates any comparison drawn across silos. Deliberately carries no tree matcher: build identity is process-scoped, so filtering by $tree would drop the series entirely.
